name: Cloud brain, local hosts: the desktop app ships no agent loop
what: The Manus Studio desktop app contains no LLM provider code and no agent loop; it supplies a local execution host (operator), an in-app browser host, and a screen-live host that a cloud agent drives through typed actions.
how: dist/ has zero matches for openai, anthropic, gemini, deepseek or chat/completions. The Electron main process spawns the Go binary manus-computer-operator with `start`, passing MANUS_OPERATOR_SOCKET_URL (the cloud chat websocket) plus a device token, so the operator dials out to the cloud and receives work. Everything model-facing (planning, prompts, tool choice) therefore sits server-side and is not visible in the shipped artifact.
evidence: grep over dist/ and @next-agent src: openai/anthropic/gemini/deepseek = 0 files
verevonRelevance: Verevon already keeps the agent loop server-side (Model Plane); the useful lesson is that a desktop app can be a pure host with outbound-only connectivity, which fits the owner rule that Quarry/endpoint code executes and the Model only proposes.
notes: The server-side half (cloud agent, planner, sandbox VM images) is not in the artifact. Direction of the executor protocol (cloud = client, operator = host) is inferred from message names ClientEnvelope/HostEnvelope/HostHello.

name: Executor protocol: one typed host protocol for operator and sandbox runtime
what: Local desktops and cloud sandboxes speak the same protobuf "executor" protocol: the cloud sends ExecuteAction envelopes (file, git, MCP, terminal, screen capture, screen live, skill catalog, wallpaper, workspace, device viewer) and the host answers with ack, progress, completed, failed or cancelled.
how: The operator binary embeds github.com/manus-ai/manus-sandbox/sbx-go-svc/executor-protocol (sdk/go/executor/v1) and sbx-go-svc/mcphost; build.json pins both module versions. Proto files seen: addon_job, common, device_addon, device_viewer, envelope, file, git, mcp_host, mcp, runtime_addon, screen_capture, screen_live, skill_catalog, terminal, transfer, wallpaper, workflow, workspace. Envelope types: ClientEnvelope{Hello, Execute, Cancel, ActionTransferAccess, DeviceAddonConfig, SessionConfig, HostCallResolved, RuntimeAddonCallAuth} and HostEnvelope{Hello, ActionAck, ActionProgress, ActionCompleted, ActionFailed, ActionCancelled, HostCallRequested, DeviceAddonConfigApplied, SessionConfigApplied, TerminalCompletionOrphaned}. Enum HostKind has OPERATOR and SANDBOX_RUNTIME, which is the direct evidence that one protocol covers both. ErrorCode includes COMMAND_LOST, HOST_UNAVAILABLE, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, PERMISSION_DENIED, TIMEOUT, CONFLICT.
evidence: install:resources/bin/manus-computer-operator.exe (binary strings): executorv1.ClientEnvelope_Execute, HostEnvelope_ActionProgress, HOST_KIND_OPERATOR, HOST_KIND_SANDBOX_RUNTIME, ERROR_CODE_COMMAND_LOST
derived list: tmp/bin/executor_msgs.txt (303 message names extracted from the operator binary)
verevonRelevance: This is the cleanest idea to copy for Verevon: define one versioned host protocol so a sandbox lease, a governed browser (Quarry) and a future endpoint all look like the same "host" to the Model Plane.
notes: Binary-strings evidence only (symbol names, no wire dumps). Field-level schema not recovered; the proto raw descriptors are gzip-embedded and could be decoded later.

name: Process model of the desktop host
what: The desktop is a small constellation of single-purpose processes rather than one monolith: Electron main/renderer, a Go operator, a Go sidecar, Rust native helpers, node-pty shells and sandboxed hidden windows.
how: Electron main (dist/index.js) -> operator (Go, named pipe JSON API) -> children: sidecar.exe (shared folder bridge), ManusComputerUseHelper.exe (Rust, stdio MCP), manus-screen-live-publisher.exe (Rust+LiveKit), manus-remote-input.exe (Rust injector, JSON lines on stdio), ManusBrowserImport.exe, node-pty shells, one utility process (utilityHostService) and addon browser workers (sandboxed BrowserWindows). REA reported 2 BrowserWindow sites, 18 explicit webPreferences and 8 sender-validation observations inside the @next-agent packages alone.

name: Wire formats chosen per link, not one RPC for everything
what: Each link uses the transport that fits it: Connect+protobuf to the cloud API, socket.io over websocket for device/terminal control, LiveKit WebRTC for pixels and human input, JSON lines over pipes/stdio for local helpers, MCP over stdio or loopback HTTP for tool servers.
how: Go operator uses internal/socketio and Connect clients (connectorsv1connect, ConnectRPC strings); Electron uses socket.io-client with transports:["websocket"] and reconnection:false (manual step timer); screen-live uses livekit-client in the renderer and livekit-ffi in the Rust publisher; the injector uses {"cmd":...} JSON lines on stdin; Browser MCP is Streamable HTTP on 127.0.0.1 with a random port.
verevonRelevance: For Verevon a Rust gateway already speaks gRPC/SSE; the point to adopt is picking a dedicated realtime data plane (LiveKit-style) for screen and human input instead of tunnelling them through the chat stream.

name: Per-launch random credentials on every local bridge
what: Every local IPC bridge is created with a fresh random secret that is handed to the one intended child through its environment, so no other local process can use the bridge.
how: Screen-live bridge: random 32-byte base64url token, per-run named pipe (win) or 0600 unix socket, 64 KiB request-line cap, token checked on every JSON line. Browser MCP: 32 random bytes hex bearer token, listens on 127.0.0.1 port 0, timing-safe comparison, token exported to the operator as MANUS_OPERATOR_BROWSER_MCP_BEARER_TOKEN. Addon browser worker tokens are HMAC-SHA256 derived per addon id and revision from a master token. Operator local API pipe name includes a random UUID.
verevonRelevance: Cheap, directly portable hardening for any Verevon local component; also shows the "capability by environment" bootstrap that avoids long-lived secrets on disk.

name: Declarative device config reconciliation for My Computer
what: The cloud pushes a versioned desired state (folders, sessions, terminal permission) to the desktop, and the desktop reconciles to it and reports an applied version plus per-session status.
how: socket.io namespace /device with auth {token, deviceId, deviceName}; server event device_config {configVersion, deviceId, folders[], sessions[]}; client replies with volatile device_status {appliedConfigVersion, sessions[], folders[], terminalAvailable}. Stale versions are ignored, updates are coalesced for 200 ms, an AbortController cancels superseded syncs, and a 10 s control-channel grace period keeps sidecars alive across blips before the runtime is cleared. SessionSupervisor starts/stops one sidecar per session, restarts only if the websocket base or folder changed, and retries with exponential backoff up to 20 attempts.
verevonRelevance: A level-triggered desired-state sync is more robust than event-by-event commands for anything that must survive reconnects; applies to Verevon sandbox leases and browser grants.
notes: This legacy-looking My Computer channel coexists with the newer operator executor path; both ship in 2.0.6.

name: Supervision of native children: serialized queue, backoff, orphan sweep, kill trees
what: The app treats native helpers as supervised services: starts are serialized, crashes restart with capped backoff, and leftovers from a previous crash are swept before a new start.
how: OperatorManager.enqueue serializes start/stop/restart; scheduleRestart uses 3 s doubling to a 10 s cap and resets the attempt counter after 30 s of uptime; the app restarts a dead operator on window focus; stopProcess kills the process group (SIGTERM then SIGKILL on unix, taskkill /T /F on Windows); orphans are removed with a PowerShell Get-CimInstance filter on ParentProcessId (run with -ExecutionPolicy Bypass); operator stdout/stderr go to operator.log capped at 10 MiB; a logout revokes the device token and stops the operator.
verevonRelevance: Standard but well executed; the focus-triggered restart and token revocation on logout are small touches worth copying.
notes: Using -ExecutionPolicy Bypass for an internal one-liner is common but would be flagged by enterprise EDR; avoid in Verevon.

name: Typed local API between Electron and the operator over a named pipe
what: The desktop UI talks to the operator through a small JSON request/notification protocol over a named pipe (unix: inherited fd 3), with explicit timeouts and an "outcome unknown" error class.
how: operatorLocalApi connects with exponential backoff (100 ms to 2 s, 10 s total), buffers up to 4 MiB, 10 s default request timeout. Methods: file.roots/locations/list/search, workspace.resolve, operator.activity_status, operator.connection_status, operator.begin_maintenance_v2, operator.cancel_maintenance, worktree.retention.*, addon.local_preview.resolve, host.ui_hint; notification remote_control_requests_changed. Mutating calls pass outcomeUnknownOnFailure and a deadlineUnixMs so a timeout surfaces as "outcome unknown, refresh before retrying".
evidence: inventory Appendix A (method list, verified against operatorLocalApi.js)
verevonRelevance: The "outcome unknown" error class plus deadline propagation is exactly what Verevon needs for approval-gated effects whose result may be lost in transit.
notes: begin_maintenance_v2 and activity_status are defined but no caller exists in dist/ (grep), so they look reserved for an installer or updater path (INF).

name: Code-mode computer use: one MCP tool, "computer-use/js", runs agent-written JavaScript against a native SDK
what: Instead of exposing a dozen click/type tools, Manus exposes a single JavaScript tool; the model writes a short script that awaits cu.<native_method>() calls, so it can batch deterministic actions and branch on results in one round trip.
how: The runtime (shared "device-javascript" package, QuickJS compiled to WASM via quickjs-emscripten 0.32.0) evaluates each cell inside an async function with no Node, filesystem, network or imports. The SDK injects globals cu (native methods plus help, budget, phase, getApp), output (write, image, observation, elements) and a persistent state object. Native calls are marshalled as JSON lines over stdio to the operator (1 MiB line cap) and results return as {text, images, isError, callIndex, structuredContent}. The same runtime also powers the in-app browser SDK (platform "browser").
verevonRelevance: Verevon lists "code mode (tools callable from the sandbox)" as absent greenfield; Manus proves a bounded QuickJS-style cell with call budget is a workable, auditable way to give a model batching without giving it a shell.
notes: Claude desktop and Codex use per-action tools; this code-cell model is rare. Efficiency claims (fewer round trips) are inferred, not measured.

name: Cell budgets, resumable state and phase accounting for scripted actions
what: Each script cell has hard resource limits and a persistent state object, and the SDK tells the model how to resume after a limit or error without replaying completed physical actions.
how: Limits: 64 native calls per cell, 38 KiB output text, 3 emitted images, default timeout 30 s (max 120 s), 64 MiB heap. State survives ordinary errors; reset, timeout, cancellation, terminal errors, helper catalog change, operator restart, session release or 30 minutes idle clear it. cu.budget() returns {limit, used, remaining, pending}; cu.phase({name, calls, reserve}, fn) refuses to start if the declared allowance does not fit and throws PHASE_CALL_LIMIT if exceeded. Errors carry code, method, callIndex, nextAction and a progress object (completedPhases, completedCallIndices, lastCompletedCall) clipped to 3 KB; the host reports statePreserved so the model knows whether locals survived. Sentinel codes: CALL_LIMIT, OUTPUT_LIMIT, ASYNC_NOT_AWAITED, PHASE_ACTIVE, CALL_BUDGET_INSUFFICIENT.
evidence: tmp/cu/guide_win32.md (embedded workflow guide, extracted from CU:2)
verevonRelevance: Directly reusable idea for Verevon Do-mode: express "do not replay completed side effects" as protocol (statePreserved, completedCallIndices) rather than only prompt text.

name: Shipped agent playbook: observe-plan-batch-verify, stop at sufficient evidence
what: The product ships a written operating procedure for the model: observe once, batch known actions, verify at decision boundaries, finish once, and do not over-verify.
how: Embedded guide text (Windows, Linux and generic are identical; macOS is longer): call computer_use_finish exactly once at the end of the whole task; use text-only observation unless a visual decision is needed; never insert discarded observations as waits; repair the failed step instead of replaying a batch; stop when the requested condition is visible; permission denial or user stop is terminal and must not be retried. The guide is emitted once by cu.getApp (bounded to 24 KiB with common schemas) so the model never has to load a skill file first.
verevonRelevance: Gives Verevon concrete prompt/contract text to benchmark against its own plan-mode and verifier loops.
notes: Guide is DOC-quality text embedded in code; its effect on model behavior is not measured here.

name: Window identity and targeting rules for Windows (HWND, PID, AUMID, path, exact title)
what: Targets are resolved through a strict ladder of identifiers and the helper refuses ambiguous app-name resolution rather than guessing.

name: Structured action receipts and tri-state verification (macOS cu.app binding)
what: On macOS the SDK offers an app-bound object whose actions return receipts separating "dispatched" from "effect verified", and unknown verification is null, never assumed success.
how: cu.app({app, activate:false}) creates a frozen binding; observe() returns {data, elements, images}; find()/findOne()/exists() return coverage {complete, truncated, visited} and throw ELEMENT_AMBIGUOUS, SEARCH_INCOMPLETE or ELEMENT_NOT_FOUND instead of picking index zero; Element handles are frozen snapshots with read()/getValue(); action results carry {method, executionMethod, dispatched, effectVerified, outcome, target, activated, warning}. Native handles live 120 s in a bounded cache and are invalidated on identity or geometry change.
verevonRelevance: Verevon verifier/proof-bundle work can adopt the dispatched versus verified split for browser and any future desktop actions.
notes: Only the macOS runtime exposes this API; Windows uses raw cu.<native> calls with the same tool names.

name: Linux and Wayland desktop control rules, with an exception for the agent own sandbox desktop
what: On Linux the agent must check readiness without requesting permissions, announce whole-screen takeover, obtain explicit Portal authorization on Wayland, and never fall back to X11/XWayland; inside the Manus Sandbox (X11) it operates without consent because it is the agent own computer.
how: addon.json description and the embedded Linux guide: Sandbox device with computer_use_status sessionType x11 is "your own computer" (user may watch or take over from the Computer panel); any other desktop, including Cloud Computer or Wayland, needs a takeover notice, request_permissions=true with capture_source=monitor, GNOME Stop Sharing as the manual revoke, and stop on cancellation without retry. Window-capture authorization is read-only. Wayland activation selectors are single-use, expire after 30 s and are invalidated on refresh.
verevonRelevance: The own-sandbox versus someone-else desktop split (consent only where a human desktop is at stake) is a clean policy rule for Verevon Space sandboxes versus any future endpoint.

name: Exactly-once side effects: action ledger keyed by (sessionUid, actionId) with payload digest and 10-minute replay horizon
what: If the same side-effect tool call arrives twice (retry, reconnect) with the same action id, the server returns the first result instead of repeating the click; a different payload under the same id is rejected as a conflict.
how: Every tool call must carry trusted _meta ai.manus/sessionUid and ai.manus/actionId. For any tool whose side-effect class is not read/read_sensitive, executeToolCall computes actionKey = len(sessionUid):sessionUid+actionId and a SHA-256 digest of canonicalized arguments (secret text masked), stores the in-flight promise in a process-local ledger for 10 minutes, returns the stored promise on identical replay, ACTION_REPLAY_CONFLICT on digest mismatch, ACTION_LEDGER_FULL when at capacity, and ACTION_IN_DOUBT when the outcome is unknown. Server instructions state the Operator action journal owns cross-process durability.
verevonRelevance: Verevon approvals already re-execute exact effects from an encrypted descriptor; adding an idempotency ledger at the Quarry boundary closes the remaining double-click-after-retry gap.
notes: Cross-process durability lives in the Go operator journal (not inspectable beyond strings).

how: Operator strings: MANUS_OPERATOR_EPOCH_RECOVERY, operatorEpochSync, "Waiting for operator startup epoch", "reading epoch file", "invalid operator epoch"; Electron restarts the operator on recorder context change and defers while a task is running.
evidence: install:resources/bin/manus-computer-operator.exe (binary strings): MANUS_OPERATOR_EPOCH_RECOVERY, "Waiting for operator startup epoch: %v"
verevonRelevance: Epoch fencing is the usual way to avoid zombie actions after host restarts; Verevon leases already have a similar concept.
notes: Low confidence on exact semantics; strings only.

name: Encrypted portal restore tokens on Linux (safeStorage, refuses plaintext backend)
what: Wayland screen-share portal restore tokens are stored encrypted with the OS keystore and the code refuses to store them when only the basic plaintext backend is available.
how: linuxPortalRestoreTokenStore writes userData/linux-portal-restore-tokens.v1.json, requires safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable() and getSelectedStorageBackend() !== basic_text, and decrypts base64 envelopes on read.
verevonRelevance: Good pattern for any Verevon endpoint that must persist a capability token: refuse insecure storage instead of falling back.
notes: File contents were not read (user data store).

name: Capability versions negotiated through bridge environment flags
what: The desktop tells the operator which bridge features exist by exporting small version flags, so an older operator or newer app can degrade instead of failing.
how: buildEnv sets MANUS_SCREENLIVE_BRIDGE_SOCKET/TOKEN, MANUS_WALLPAPER_BRIDGE_VERSION=1, MANUS_OPERATOR_BROWSER_ALLOWED_HOSTS=1, MANUS_OPERATOR_BROWSER_TEMPORARY_INPUT=2, MANUS_OPERATOR_LOCAL_ADDONS=1, MANUS_OPERATOR_PLATFORM=desktop; the computer-use runtime says "Update the Computer Use helper; structured result missing" when a helper lacks structuredContent.
verevonRelevance: A cheap compatibility handshake worth adding to any Verevon host-to-plane link.
